item.title: 4. Green for an empty reason
item.description:
Europe's €525 million chip design platform, Empyrean's bid for EasyLogic, UC San Diego and Qualcomm's AI-for-design initiative and Silvaco's agentic claims, an explainer on vacuity built around the 'Verified but Vacuous' paper, and a verification corner on an Arm engineer's study in which three AI agents hit 100% of their own coverage goals and signed off with bugs still in the design.

Sources:

  • EU €525 million investment set to drive new generation of European chip design companies (European Commission)
  • EU launches €525 million chip design platform for start-ups and SMEs (Commission press text, republished)
  • Synopsys expands access to advanced chip design capabilities through European Chips Design Platform (EEJournal)
  • Huawei partner Empyrean buys Chinese chip design startup (Seoul Economic Daily)
  • Empyrean proposes buying 50.38% of EasyLogic for CNY 218.8 million (Neoteo)
  • UC San Diego launches AI-driven chip design research initiative supported by Qualcomm Technologies (UC San Diego)
  • Silvaco third quarter 2026 results, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC)
  • Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation (arXiv)
  • Putting AI To The Test (Semiconductor Engineering, Brian Bailey)
  • ICCAD 2026
  • Synopsys announces earnings release date for fourth quarter and fiscal year 2026 (Synopsys)

Researched and written by Claude; voiced with synthetic speech.

item.title: 3. Trained against the tools
item.description:
Cadence's Maestro models and Q3 results, ChipAgents moving into analog with fine-tuned Nemotron models, a deep dive on training AI against EDA tools and why the grader is the part to watch, and a verification corner on Harmonic's Aristotle proving properties of Verilog.

  • Cadence Q3 2026 financial results, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC)
  • Cadence Q3 FY 2026: AI agents expand design workflow adoption (Futurum)
  • ChipAgents expands full-stack agentic AI across digital and analog chip design (ChipAgents)

item.title: 2. Proving nothing changed
item.description:
Siemens and NVIDIA's agent-run 3D-IC thermal workflow, Cadence's sovereign AI platform and Nokia's 5x claim, VerifierBench on AI-written checkers, an explainer on equivalence checking, and a verification corner on why 100% coverage isn't proof the data was right.

item.title: 1. Spec to layout: how far can agents get?
item.description:
